narrative: Markets are navigating severe turbulence in the technology sector following the abrupt resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid an internal probe, potential trade secret espionage investigations, and possible US entity listing risks. While tech sentiment is rattled, the upcoming six-times oversubscribed Anthropic IPO and Nvidia's Q3 earnings are seen as pivotal tests for AI capital expenditure and valuation sustainability. Broader equities are partially buffered by resilient US consumer strength and ongoing global fund inflows, though geopolitical friction between the US and China alongside Middle East instability remains acute. Meanwhile, macroeconomic focus is shifting toward rising AI debt accumulation, non-bank financial leverage, and potential tightening of export controls.

Nasdaq.view: Under pressure and down 10% from highs, weighed down by the Nvidia leadership crisis, US-China chip export risks, and heavy selling across semiconductors as noted by Barry Ritholtz and Charlie Pellet.

S&P 500.view: Tony Crescenzi expects growth supported by consumer resilience and data centers, but Charlie Pellet and Richard Haass note drag from tech weakness and corporate governance uncertainty keeping the index off record highs.

Gold.view: Trading little changed around $38.78/oz according to Charlie Pellet, while George Alexander Muthoot highlights Indian households holding roughly 35,000 tons of gold as vital loan collateral.

Oil.view: WTI and Brent faced selling pressure heading into the weekend, though Tara Copp and Eimear Bonner point out supportive geopolitical risks in the Middle East alongside Chevron ramping Venezuelan output to nearly 300,000 bpd.
